PC-OTH-014.explanation: Fair Access to Insurance Requirements plans are residual market associations, set up by law and funded by insurers, that provide basic property insurance to owners who cannot buy it in the voluntary market. In Georgia every insurer writing property insurance must belong to the FAIR Plan underwriting association (O.C.G.A. 33-33-3). Automobile assigned risk plans serve high-risk drivers.

PC-GEN-024.question: An insurer incorporated in Canada and licensed to do business in Georgia is classified in Georgia as a(n):
PC-GEN-024.explanation: O.C.G.A. 33-3-1 defines an alien insurer as one formed under the laws of a country other than the United States. A foreign insurer is formed in another U.S. state, and a domestic insurer is formed under Georgia law.

PC-AUTO-017.explanation: Georgia folds underinsured protection into uninsured motorist coverage: under O.C.G.A. 33-7-11(b)(1)(D)(ii) an at-fault vehicle whose liability insurance is too small for the insured's damages is treated as uninsured, and by default the UM limits pay on top of that liability coverage. A driver with no insurance at all is the classic uninsured case, not an underinsured one.
